title: Accounting for Partnership Firms: Fundamentals
summary: This chapter covers the nature of partnership, the partnership deed and the rules of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 that apply when there is no deed. It explains fixed and fluctuating capital accounts, the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account, interest on capital and drawings, guarantee of profit and the correction of past adjustments.

notes.heading: Meaning and features of partnership
notes.html:
Section 4 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 describes partnership as the relation between persons who have agreed to share the profits of a business carried on by all of them or by any of them acting for all. The persons are individually called partners and collectively a firm; the name under which business is done is the firm name.

  • Two or more persons: minimum 2. The maximum is 50, prescribed under Section 464 of the Companies Act, 2013 read with Rule 10 of the Companies (Miscellaneous) Rules, 2014.
  • Agreement: the relation arises from an agreement (oral or written), not from status or inheritance.
  • Lawful business: the agreement must be to carry on a lawful business; joint ownership of property alone is not partnership.
  • Sharing of profits: partners agree to share profits (and, by implication, losses).
  • Mutual agency: each partner is an agent of the firm and of the other partners. This is the real test of partnership.
  • Unlimited liability: partners are jointly and severally liable for the debts of the firm.

notes.heading: Partnership deed and rules when there is no deed
notes.html:
The partnership deed is the written agreement containing the terms of partnership: name and address of the firm and partners, nature of business, capital contributed, profit-sharing ratio, interest on capital and drawings, salary or commission to partners, rules for admission, retirement, death and dissolution, method of valuing goodwill and settlement of disputes.

When the deed is absent, or silent on a point, the following provisions of the Act apply:

MatterRule in absence of deed
Profit-sharing ratioEqual
Interest on capitalNot allowed
Interest on drawingsNot charged
Salary, commission or other remuneration to a partnerNot allowed
Interest on a loan or advance given by a partner (over and above capital)6% p.a. [Section 13(d)]; it is a charge and is allowed even if the firm suffers a loss
Admission of a new partnerOnly with the consent of all existing partners

Exam tip: if a question says the deed is silent, apply this table strictly; do not allow interest on capital or salary even if a partner 'claims' it.

notes.heading: Capital accounts: fixed and fluctuating methods
notes.html:
Fixed capital method: each partner has two accounts. The Capital Account records only the opening capital and permanent additions or withdrawals, so its balance normally stays the same. All other items go to the Current Account, which may show a debit or a credit balance.

Fluctuating capital method: only one Capital Account is kept; all items are recorded in it, so the balance changes every year. If the question is silent, capitals are taken as fluctuating.

Debit side of Current (or Capital) AccountCredit side of Current (or Capital) Account
DrawingsBalance b/d (credit)
Interest on drawingsInterest on capital
Share of lossSalary or commission to partner
Balance c/dShare of profit
BasisFixed capitalFluctuating capital
Number of accountsTwo: capital and currentOne: capital only
BalanceCapital balance unchanged unless capital is added or withdrawnChanges every year
Debit balanceCapital account always shows a credit balance; current account may be debitCapital account may show a debit balance
Adjustments recorded inCurrent accountCapital account

notes.heading: Profit and Loss Appropriation Account
notes.html:
The P&L Appropriation Account is an extension of the Profit and Loss Account. It shows how the net profit is distributed among partners. Items here are appropriations of profit, not charges against profit.

Dr. ParticularsCr. Particulars
To Interest on Capital (each partner)By Profit and Loss A/c (net profit b/d)
To Partner's Salary / CommissionBy Interest on Drawings (each partner)
To General Reserve (transfer)By Partners' Capital/Current A/cs (if net loss is divided)
To Profit transferred to Partners' Capital/Current A/cs (in profit-sharing ratio)

Charge vs appropriation: interest on a partner's loan, rent paid to a partner for his premises and a manager's (employee's) commission are charges and are debited to the Profit and Loss Account, not to the Appropriation Account.

Worked illustration 1

A and B share profits 3:2. Capitals: A ₹5,00,000, B ₹3,00,000. Interest on capital 10% p.a.; B gets salary ₹5,000 per month; interest on drawings: A ₹3,000, B ₹2,000. Net profit before these items ₹2,40,000.

Dr. Particulars₹Cr. Particulars₹
To Interest on Capital: A 50,000; B 30,00080,000By Profit and Loss A/c2,40,000
To B's Salary (5,000 x 12)60,000By Interest on Drawings: A 3,000; B 2,0005,000
To Profit: A (3/5) 63,000; B (2/5) 42,0001,05,000
Total2,45,000Total2,45,000

Divisible profit = 2,40,000 + 5,000 − 80,000 − 60,000 = ₹1,05,000.

notes.heading: Interest on capital
notes.html:
• Allowed only if the deed provides for it. It is calculated on the opening capital for the full year, and on additional capital for the period it remained in the business; capital withdrawn reduces the interest from the date of withdrawal.
  • If the deed is silent on whether interest is a charge, it is an appropriation and is allowed only out of profits:
    • Profit more than total interest: allow full interest.
    • Profit less than total interest: distribute the available profit in the ratio of interest on capital.
    • Loss: no interest is allowed.
  • If the deed says interest on capital is to be treated as a charge, it is allowed in full even if the result is a loss.
  • If opening capital is not given, find it: Opening capital = Closing capital + Drawings − Share of profit (and other credits) + Share of loss (and other debits) − Fresh capital introduced.

Example: X and Y have capitals of ₹4,00,000 and ₹2,00,000; interest 10% p.a.; profit ₹30,000. Total interest = 40,000 + 20,000 = ₹60,000, which is more than profit. Profit is shared in the ratio of interest 2:1, so X gets ₹20,000 and Y ₹10,000 as interest; nothing is left to distribute.

notes.heading: Interest on drawings
notes.html:
Charged only if the deed provides. If the rate is given 'per annum', interest is calculated for the time the money was withdrawn; if given as a flat rate with no time ('5% on drawings'), charge it for the whole amount without time.

Pattern of drawings (equal amounts)Average period (months)
Beginning of each month6.5
Middle of each month6
End of each month5.5
Beginning of each quarter7.5
End of each quarter4.5
Date not known / evenly through the year6

Interest = Total drawings x Rate/100 x Average period/12.

Product method (unequal amounts on different dates): multiply each drawing by the months from its date to the end of the year, add the products and apply: Interest = Sum of products x Rate/100 x 1/12.

Worked illustration 2

A draws ₹10,000 at the beginning of every month; rate 6% p.a. Total drawings ₹1,20,000. Interest = 1,20,000 x 6/100 x 6.5/12 = ₹3,900. If drawn at the end of each month: 1,20,000 x 6/100 x 5.5/12 = ₹3,300; in the middle: ₹3,600.

Worked illustration 3 (product method)

M withdrew on 1 June ₹10,000; 1 September ₹15,000; 1 December ₹5,000; 1 March ₹20,000. Year ends 31 March; rate 9% p.a.

1 June10,000101,00,000
1 September15,00071,05,000
1 December5,000420,000
1 March20,000120,000
Total50,0002,45,000

Interest = 2,45,000 x 9/100 x 1/12 = ₹1,837.50.

notes.heading: Guarantee of profit to a partner
notes.html:
A partner (usually a new or junior one) may be guaranteed a minimum amount of profit. If his actual share is less, the deficiency is borne by:

  • The firm: all other partners bear it in their profit-sharing ratio (unless agreed otherwise).
  • One or some partners: only the guaranteeing partner(s) bear it, in the agreed ratio.

Worked illustration 4

X, Y and Z share profits 3:2:1. Z is guaranteed a minimum of ₹50,000 by the firm. Profit ₹2,40,000.

PartnerNormal share ₹Deficiency borne ₹Final share ₹
X (3/6)1,20,000(6,000)1,14,000
Y (2/6)80,000(4,000)76,000
Z (1/6)40,000+10,00050,000
Total2,40,000Nil2,40,000

Deficiency = 50,000 − 40,000 = ₹10,000, borne by X and Y in 3:2. If the guarantee were given by X alone, X would bear the whole ₹10,000 (X ₹1,10,000; Y ₹80,000; Z ₹50,000).

notes.heading: Past adjustments
notes.html:
When errors or omissions of earlier years (for example, interest on capital or salary omitted, or profits shared in a wrong ratio) are discovered after accounts are closed, they are corrected through the partners' capital/current accounts with a single adjusting entry, without reopening old accounts.

  1. Prepare a table with a column for each partner.
  2. Credit each partner with what he should have received (e.g. interest on capital omitted).
  3. Debit each partner with what he must give back (the same total, in profit-sharing ratio, because profit was over-distributed).
  4. Net effect: partners with a net debit are debited; those with a net credit are credited.

Worked illustration 5

A, B and C (fixed capitals ₹3,00,000, ₹2,00,000 and ₹1,00,000) shared profit of ₹1,20,000 equally, but interest on capital @ 6% p.a. was omitted.

ParticularsA ₹B ₹C ₹Total ₹
Interest on capital (Cr)18,00012,0006,00036,000
Profit taken back equally (Dr)(12,000)(12,000)(12,000)(36,000)
Net effect6,000 CrNil6,000 DrNil

Entry: C's Current A/c Dr ₹6,000 To A's Current A/c ₹6,000.

notes.heading: Common mistakes to avoid
notes.html:
• Debiting interest on a partner's loan to the Appropriation Account; it is a charge in the Profit and Loss Account.
  • Allowing interest on capital in a loss year when the deed treats it as an appropriation.
  • Calculating interest on drawings for 12 months instead of the average period.
  • Forgetting that commission 'on net profit after charging such commission' = Profit before commission x Rate/(100 + Rate).
  • Recording drawings, salary and interest in the capital account when capitals are fixed; they belong to the current account.
  • In past adjustments, passing separate entries for each item when one net entry is required.

keyTerms.definition: Relation between persons who agree to share the profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all (Section 4, Partnership Act, 1932).
Written agreement containing the terms and conditions of partnership; it should be properly stamped.
Each partner acts both as an agent and as a principal of the firm; the real test of partnership.
Method under which each partner has a Capital A/c (permanent capital only) and a Current A/c (all other adjustments).
Method under which all adjustments are recorded in a single capital account, so its balance keeps changing.
Account prepared after the Profit and Loss Account to show distribution of net profit among partners.
Return allowed to partners on capital contributed; an appropriation of profit unless the deed treats it as a charge.
Interest charged from partners on amounts withdrawn; it is a gain to the firm and is credited to the Appropriation Account.
Assurance of a minimum amount of profit to a partner; any deficiency is borne by the guaranteeing partner(s) or the firm.
Corrections of omissions or errors of earlier years made through partners' capital/current accounts by one adjusting entry.
Profit left after all appropriations such as interest on capital, salary, commission and transfer to reserve; shared in profit-sharing ratio.

formulas.name: Interest on drawings (equal amounts)
formulas.html: Total drawings x Rate/100 x Average period/12 (average period: 6.5 beginning, 6 middle, 5.5 end of month; 7.5 beginning, 4.5 end of quarter)

formulas.name: Interest on drawings (product method)
formulas.html: Sum of (Drawing x Months outstanding) x Rate/100 x 1/12

formulas.name: Commission on profit after charging commission
formulas.html: Net profit before commission x Rate/(100 + Rate)

formulas.name: Commission on profit before charging commission
formulas.html: Net profit before commission x Rate/100

formulas.name: Opening capital
formulas.html: Closing capital + Drawings + Interest on drawings + Share of loss − Share of profit − Interest on capital − Salary/commission − Additional capital introduced

formulas.name: Divisible profit
formulas.html: Net profit + Interest on drawings − Interest on capital − Salary/commission to partners − Transfer to reserve

formulas.name: Deficiency on guarantee
formulas.html: Guaranteed amount − Actual share of profit of the guaranteed partner

mcqs.q: In the absence of a partnership deed, a partner who has advanced a loan to the firm is entitled to interest at:
mcqs.explanation: Section 13(d) of the Partnership Act, 1932 allows interest at 6% p.a. on a partner's loan, even if the firm earns no profit.

mcqs.q: The maximum number of partners permitted in a partnership firm under the Companies Act, 2013 and the related Rules is:
mcqs.explanation: Rule 10 of the Companies (Miscellaneous) Rules, 2014, made under Section 464, fixes the limit at 50 partners.

mcqs.q: A partner withdrew ₹4,000 at the beginning of every month. Interest on drawings is charged @ 10% p.a. The interest for the year will be:
mcqs.explanation: Total drawings ₹48,000; average period 6.5 months. 48,000 x 10/100 x 6.5/12 = ₹2,600.

mcqs.q:
Assertion (A): Interest on a partner's loan is debited to the Profit and Loss Account and not to the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account.
Reason (R): Interest on a partner's loan is a charge against profit.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Interest on loan must be paid whether or not there is profit; being a charge, it is debited to the Profit and Loss Account. R explains A.

mcqs.q: Case: P and Q are partners with capitals of ₹4,00,000 and ₹2,00,000. The deed allows interest on capital @ 10% p.a. but is silent on whether it is a charge. The firm's profit for the year is ₹30,000. P's interest on capital will be:
mcqs.explanation: Total interest ₹60,000 exceeds profit, so the profit of ₹30,000 is shared in the ratio of interest 40,000 : 20,000 = 2:1. P gets ₹20,000.

mcqs.q: When capitals are fixed, salary payable to a partner is credited to the partner's:
mcqs.explanation: Under the fixed capital method, all items other than permanent capital changes are recorded in the current account.

mcqs.q: The manager of a firm is entitled to a commission of 10% of net profit after charging such commission. Net profit before commission is ₹1,32,000. The commission will be:
X, Y and Z share profits 2:2:1. Z is guaranteed a minimum profit of ₹30,000 and the deficiency is to be borne by X alone. Profit for the year is ₹1,00,000. X's final share of profit is:
mcqs.explanation: Z's normal share = ₹20,000; deficiency ₹10,000 is borne by X. X = 40,000 − 10,000 = ₹30,000.

mcqs.q: If equal amounts are withdrawn at the end of each quarter, interest on drawings is calculated for an average period of:
mcqs.explanation: Amounts are outstanding for 9, 6, 3 and 0 months; average = 18/4 = 4.5 months.

mcqs.q:
Assertion (A): In the absence of a deed, a working partner is entitled to a salary for managing the business.
Reason (R): The Partnership Act allows remuneration to a partner only if there is an agreement to that effect.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
mcqs.explanation: No salary is allowed without an agreement, so A is false; R correctly states the law.

mcqs.q: A and B (capitals ₹2,00,000 and ₹1,00,000) share profits equally. Interest on capital @ 5% p.a. was omitted after accounts were closed. The adjusting entry will be:
mcqs.explanation: Interest: A ₹10,000, B ₹5,000 (total ₹15,000), recovered equally ₹7,500 each. Net: A +2,500, B −2,500; so debit B and credit A ₹2,500.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is debited to the Profit and Loss Account and NOT to the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account?
options: Rent paid to a partner for use of his premises
mcqs.explanation: Rent to a partner is a business expense (charge); the other three are appropriations of profit.

questions.q: State the rate of interest allowed on a loan advanced by a partner to the firm when there is no partnership deed.
questions.answerHtml: Interest is allowed @ 6% per annum as per Section 13(d) of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, even if there is a loss.

questions.q: Give any two items that are credited to a partner's current account under the fixed capital method.
questions.answerHtml:
• Interest on capital
  • Salary / commission to the partner (also share of profit)
